papers.summary: Based on the analysis of 96 organizational innovation in healthcare (OIH) projects and 52 interviews conducted with project leaders initiating these innovations, this research identifies the phenomena underlying the genesis of OIHs. The results highlight the major role played by factors such as patient empathy, international inspiration, academic inspiration, technological inspiration, serendipitous encounters, and the desire for organizational transformation in driving the generation of OIHs. Furthermore, our findings emphasize the dual nature of the research and development process for these innovations, characterized as both ex nihilo and ex materia.

papers.authors: Fatima Yatim, Alan Sitkin, Cadenza Academic Translations
papers.summary: This article explores the dynamics of collaborative and participatory innovations in public health services using Chen et al.’s (2020) typology. Based on a mixed survey of projects awarded under the national “Droits des usagers de la santé” initiative, the study finds that user participation primarily generates operational and capacity-oriented innovations frequently involving external partnerships. The analysis highlights the crucial interactions between internal and external dynamics, identifying essential conditions for successful innovations: effective mobilization of internal resources, robust institutional support, and early and active user involvement. However, the study also identifies limitations in citizen engagement, particularly in the evaluation phase of innovations. The article concludes by suggesting avenues for enhancing full co-creation processes in public services to maximize public value.

papers.title_ja: 地方自治体における環境管理制御の性質とテンション
papers.authors: Christophe Maurel, Christophe Favoreu, London Proofreaders
papers.summary: This exploratory research aims to characterize, on the one hand, the concept of environmental management control (EMC) through the practices that underpin it, and, on the other hand, the tensions associated with it and the implementation of these practices in public organizations. Although EMC is attracting growing interest within the public sector, it seems to be facing technical and governance difficulties. A grid for analyzing management tools and the theory of organizational paradoxes is used to address the issue of characterizing EMC practices and the associated tensions in the local public sector. Various municipalities were mobilized to explore and characterize their first experiences of implementing EMC. Our results enable us to characterize both the tools used and the tensions generated between the objectives pursued in terms of resource management, dialogue with the socio-economic environment, and behavioral orientation.

papers.title: The Role of Collective Bricolage in Creating University Governance Structures: The Example of the Galileo Observatory
papers.title_ja: 大学ガバナンス構造創造における集団的ブリコラージュの役割：ガリレオ天文台の事例
papers.summary: This study investigates the concept of “collective bricolage” within the framework of creating a universe science observatory in France. In the face of significant transformations in higher education and research, this article examines how university stakeholders can employ collective bricolage to adapt to institutional mandates for restructuring. Drawing on Lévi-Strauss’s notion of bricolage and the theoretical contributions of Duymedjian and Rüling (2010), this research investigates how this bricolage can be implemented in the absence of conventional or normative space to support the process, and particularly within a context characterized by conflictual relationships. The case study analyzes the collective bricolage process and its components, demonstrating that the dialectical nature of collective bricolage facilitates the creation of robust governance structures through the negotiation and recombination of resources and rationales from the diverse actors involved.

papers.summary: In this transformative study, Simon Smith explores how playwrights like Shakespeare crafted their plays for demanding and varied commercial audiences. Rediscovering the many forms of judgement practiced in the early modern playhouse, he investigates influences ranging from the classical tradition and grammar-school classroom to ballad and jest culture. Where many prior studies have treated 'the judicious' as a self-contained subset of playgoers, Smith reveals the variety of careful assessments made in the theatre by a wide range of playgoers, showing that judgement and pleasure were often simultaneous elements of the same response. Chapters examine specific parts of plays that were especially subject to evaluation and generative of enjoyment: spectacle, words, plot, and actorly technique. Close readings shed fresh light on much-studied plays like Hamlet and Volpone, as well as exploring several unfairly overlooked plays. papers.title: Roman Polanski after The Pianist: The Man and His Films
papers.title_ja: 『ピアニスト』以後のロマン・ポランスキー：人間と映画
papers.summary: Roman Polanski after The Pianist examines Polanski’s later films as a distinct and coherent phase in his career. Situating these works within changing industrial, cultural and political conditions, the book shows how Polanski’s late cinema rethinks genre, sound, work, domestic space and historical memory. Drawing on production studies, sound analysis and theories of authorship and mediation, it explores the formal strategies through which these films construct their cinematic worlds. Engaging contemporary debates on art, morality and authorship, the authors argue for the critical autonomy of artworks in a culture increasingly shaped by biographical scrutiny and moral judgement.
